title: Adjoining an n-th root of an element with unit derivative preserves regularity
statement: Let $R$ be a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (Noetherian, every localization at a prime a regular local ring), let $f\in R$, and let $D:R\to R$ be a derivation (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) such that $D(f)$ is a unit of $R$. Then for every integer $n\ge1$ the ring $R[z]/(z^n-f)$, the quotient of the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring] by the ideal generated by $z^n-f$, is a regular ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PG (lemma-degree-p-extension-regular, line 11844), first sentence, and its proof (Algebra Lemma 07NF regular-goes-up: R[z] regular; Lemma 07PF quotient-regular applied to the extension of D with D(z) = 0)
